cues: A student can know every treaty in the history book and still quarrel with a classmate for a year over a borrowed pen.
A scientist can understand the atom perfectly and still build something that frightens the world.
In nineteen fifty four, Bertrand Russell asked why our knowledge has grown so fast while our wisdom has not.
